claim: Cartilaginous structures are at the core of embryo growth and shaping before the bone forms.
source: Cartilaginous structures are at the core of embryo growth and shaping before the bone forms.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that establishes the importance of cartilage in embryonic development.

claim: A novel principle of vertebrate cartilage growth is based on introducing transversally-oriented clones into pre-existing cartilage.
source: Here we report a novel principle of vertebrate cartilage growth that is based on introducing transversally-oriented clones into pre-existing cartilage.
evidence: This is the main finding reported in the abstract, representing a primary discovery of the study.

claim: The mechanism of growth uncouples the lateral expansion of curved cartilaginous sheets from the control of cartilage thickness.
source: This mechanism of growth uncouples the lateral expansion of curved cartilaginous sheets from the control of cartilage thickness, a process which might be the evolutionary mechanism underlying adaptations of facial shape.
evidence: This claim describes a functional consequence of the discovered growth mechanism, supported by experimental observations.

claim: This process might be the evolutionary mechanism underlying adaptations of facial shape.
source: This mechanism of growth uncouples the lateral expansion of curved cartilaginous sheets from the control of cartilage thickness, a process which might be the evolutionary mechanism underlying adaptations of facial shape.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary implications of the discovered mechanism.

claim: In rod-shaped cartilage structures (Meckel, ribs and skeletal elements in developing limbs), the transverse integration of clonal columns determines the well-defined diameter and resulting rod-like morphology.
source: In rod-shaped cartilage structures (Meckel, ribs and skeletal elements in developing limbs), the transverse integration of clonal columns determines the well-defined diameter and resulting rod-like morphology.
evidence: This claim extends the main finding to rod-shaped cartilage structures, supported by experimental data.

claim: Cartilage shape can be altered by experimentally manipulating clonal geometries.
source: We were able to alter cartilage shape by experimentally manipulating clonal geometries.
evidence: This claim describes an experimental manipulation that validates the functional importance of clonal geometries.

claim: Anisotropic proliferation might explain cartilage bending and groove formation at the macro-scale.
source: Using in silico modeling, we discovered that anisotropic proliferation might explain cartilage bending and groove formation at the macro-scale.
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling results.

claim: Cartilage is an essential skeletal and supportive tissue in our body.
source: Cartilage is an essential skeletal and supportive tissue in our body.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The shape and size of each cartilage element results from complex developmental processes involving mesenchymal cell condensation, differentiation into chondrocytes, and orchestrated growth.
source: The shape and size of each cartilage element results from complex developmental processes; mesenchymal cells initially condensate, differentiate into chondrocytes, and then an orchestrated growth of the entire structure occurs (Goldring et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Cartilage often plays an important role as a developmental intermediate, such as during the endochondral growth of the long-bones.
source: Often, cartilage plays an important role as a developmental intermediate, such as during the endochondral growth of the long-bones (Mackie et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Cartilage elements vary widely in their shapes, including simple shapes like rods or bars and sheet-like structures, as well as extremely complicated irregular shapes.
source: Cartilage elements vary widely in their shapes: they may be simple shapes like rods or bars (Meckel, cartilage templates of the future long bones and ribs) or sheet-like structures (in the head), but can be extremely complicated with a huge number of irregular shapes (for instance, in the inner ear or pelvis).
evidence: This is a descriptive statement based on anatomical knowledge.

claim: The geometrical properties of cartilage elements must be fine-tuned during growth because cartilage provides indispensable structural support to the body during development.
source: The geometrical properties of cartilage elements must be fine-tuned during the growth because cartilage provides indispensable structural support to the body during development.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the functional role of cartilage.

claim: How cartilage geometry is fine-tuned during growth despite drastic changes in size is unclear.
source: Yet, how this is achieved despite drastic changes in size is unclear.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: After early cartilage forms from mesenchymal condensations, growth typically occurs in all dimensions.
source: After early cartilage forms from mesenchymal condensations, growth typically occurs in all dimensions.
evidence: This is a general statement about cartilage growth based on existing knowledge.

claim: The diversity of cell dynamics controlling precise early growth and shaping is not well studied.
source: However, the diversity of cell dynamics controlling precise early growth and shaping is not well studied.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in the literature.

claim: The late growth of long rod-shaped cartilage elements in limbs is achieved through a mechanism of endochondral ossification that includes oriented cell dynamics in growth plate-like zones.
source: At the same time, the late growth of long rod-shaped cartilage elements in limbs is achieved through a mechanism of endochondral ossification that includes oriented cell dynamics in growth plate-like zones (Vortkamp et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In the germinal zone of a growth plate, chondrocytes proliferate and produce progenies that form long streams oriented along the main axis of the forming skeletal element.
source: In the germinal zone of a growth plate, chondrocytes proliferate and produce progenies that form long streams oriented along the main axis of the forming skeletal element.
evidence: This is a description of known growth plate biology.

claim: Inside growth plate streams, chondrocytes undergo flattening, oriented cell divisions and hypertrophy before dissipating and giving place to the forming bone.
source: Inside such streams, chondrocytes undergo flattening, oriented cell divisions and hypertrophy before dissipating and giving place to the forming bone (Nilsson et al., 2005), a process which is controlled by many signals (Kronenberg, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Growth plate cell dynamics enable efficient extension of the skeletal element in a specific direction that coincides with the orientation of cell divisions in the proliferative zone.
source: This cell dynamic enables efficient extension of the skeletal element in a specific direction that coincides with the orientation of cell divisions in the proliferative zone (Abad et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Growth plate disorders may result in dwarfism and other illnesses.
source: Growth plate disorders may result in dwarfism and other illnesses (De Luca, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Some parts of the cartilaginous skull (e.g. the basisphenoid of the chondrocranium) undergo endochondrial ossification in synchondroses.
source: Some parts of the cartilaginous skull (e.g. the basisphenoid of the chondrocranium) also undergo endochondrial ossification in synchondroses, and significant growth of the cranial base is achieved through a similar mechanism (Hari et al., 2012; Wealthall and Herring, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Synchondroses are mirror-image growth plates arising in the cranial base, which primarily facilitate growth in the anterio-posterior direction.
source: Synchondroses are mirror-image growth plates arising in the cranial base, which primarily facilitate growth in the anterio-posterior direction (Kettunen et al., 2006; Laurita et al., 2011; Nagayama et al., 2008; Young et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Disorders in the development of synchondroses severely impact the elongation of the cranial base and often result in short-faced mutants and a general decrease of the cranial length.
source: Disorders in the development of synchondroses severely impact the elongation of the cranial base and often result in short-faced mutants and a general decrease of the cranial length (Ford-Hutchinson et al., 2007; Ma and Lozanoff, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Insufficient or abnormal development of a cartilage element is one of the reasons for human craniofacial pathologies, providing a connection between the chondrocranium and facial bone geometry, size and placement.
source: Insufficient or abnormal development of a cartilage element is one of the reasons for human craniofacial pathologies, providing a connection between the chondrocranium and facial bone geometry, size and placement (Wang et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The growth mechanism operating in growth plates and synchondroses involves the transformation of the cartilage into the bone.
source: The growth mechanism operating in growth plates and synchondroses involves the transformation of the cartilage into the bone.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge of skeletal development.

claim: Since growth plates or synchondroses are oriented towards a specific direction, the expansion of a cartilage in other dimensions is not clear from the mechanistic point of view and requires further investigation.
source: Since growth plates or synchondroses are oriented towards a specific direction, the expansion of a cartilage in other dimensions is not clear from the mechanistic point of view and requires further investigation.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: The mouse chondrocranium develops as 14 independent pairs of cartilage elements that form one united structure.
source: For example, although it is well known that the mouse chondrocranium develops as 14 independent pairs of cartilage elements that form one united structure, the logic behind further shaping and scaling remains unclear (Hari et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: How initially separated large cartilaginous elements form, grow and fine-tune their geometry, thickness and smoothness during development is still not completely understood.
source: How these initially separated large cartilaginous elements form, grow and fine-tune their geometry, thickness and smoothness during development is still not completely understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: Accurate cartilage growth might require alternative cell dynamics that do not involve hypertrophy, ossification or growth plates.
source: We hypothesized that accurate cartilage growth might require alternative cell dynamics that do not involve hypertrophy, ossification or growth plates.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated by the authors.

claim: Alternative cell dynamics may contribute to the accuracy of scaling during cartilage growth.
source: Such alternative cell dynamics may also contribute to the accuracy of scaling during cartilage growth.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential role of alternative cell dynamics.

claim: Scaling is a process of growth that maintains both the shape and the proportions of the overall structure.
source: Scaling is a process of growth that maintains both the shape and the proportions of the overall structure.
evidence: This is a definition based on established biological concepts.

claim: In nature, scaling often involves sophisticated principles of directional growth and a number of feedback mechanisms.
source: In nature, scaling often involves sophisticated principles of directional growth and a number of feedback mechanisms (Green et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: During bird development, the diversity in beak shape is constrained by the dynamics of proliferative zones in the anterior face.
source: For instance, during bird development, the diversity in beak shape is constrained by the dynamics of proliferative zones in the anterior face (Fritz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Scaling variations of beaks with the same basic shape result from signaling that controls the growth of the pre-nasal cartilage and the pre-maxillary bone.
source: Furthermore, scaling variations of beaks with the same basic shape result from signaling that controls the growth of the pre-nasal cartilage and the pre-maxillary bone (Mallarino et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In order to accurately scale a pre-shaped 3D-cartilaginous template both local isotropic and anisotropic cell dynamics may be required.
source: Indeed, in order to accurately scale a pre-shaped 3D-cartilaginous template both local isotropic and anisotropic cell dynamics may be required.
evidence: This is an inference based on the complexity of 3D scaling.

claim: The study used micro-computed tomography (μ-CT), genetic tracing with multicolor reporter mouse strains, multiple mutants and mathematical modelling to assess changes in the complete 3D anatomy of the face.
source: To assess changes in the complete 3D anatomy of the face following cellular-level mechanistic studies we used a variety of approaches including micro-computed tomography (μ-CT), genetic tracing with multicolor reporter mouse strains, multiple mutants and mathematical modelling.
evidence: This describes the methodological approaches used in the study.

claim: Oriented clonal behavior in the chondrogenic lineage controls the overall geometry of the cartilage elements.
source: Most importantly, we reveal here how oriented clonal behavior in the chondrogenic lineage controls the overall geometry of the cartilage elements, and show that this geometry can be manipulated with molecular tools at various levels.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study.

claim: Cartilage geometry can be manipulated with molecular tools at various levels.
source: Most importantly, we reveal here how oriented clonal behavior in the chondrogenic lineage controls the overall geometry of the cartilage elements, and show that this geometry can be manipulated with molecular tools at various levels.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study demonstrating experimental manipulation.

claim: The developing face provides a remarkable variety of cartilage geometries and sizes and may serve as a sophisticated model system to study the induction of complex cartilaginous structures.
source: The developing face provides a remarkable variety of cartilage geometries and sizes and, therefore, may serve as a sophisticated model system to study the induction of complex cartilaginous structures.
evidence: This is a rationale for using the facial cartilage as a model system.

claim: The developing cartilaginous skull, the chondrocranium, displays a very complex geometry of mostly sheet-like cartilages that result from coordinated anisotropic growth in all dimensions.
source: The developing cartilaginous skull, the chondrocranium, displays a very complex geometry of mostly sheet-like cartilages that result from coordinated anisotropic growth in all dimensions.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about chondrocranium development.

claim: Expansion of sheet-like cartilaginous tissue during embryonic development involves several mechanisms including the formation and growth of cartilage at synchondroses, as well as at the apical growth zone.
source: Such expansion of sheet-like cartilaginous tissue during embryonic development involves several mechanisms that were proposed in the past, including the formation and growth of cartilage at synchondroses, as well as at the apical growth zone.
evidence: This statement summarizes previously proposed mechanisms.

claim: 3D reconstructions using μ-CT enhanced with soft tissue contrasting enable the identification of various tissues and cell types in the embryo based on differential uptake of tungsten ions.
source: To understand the changes in dimensions of chondrocranium growth at major developmental stages, we took advantage of 3D reconstructions using μ-CT enhanced with soft tissue contrasting (Figure 1). This approach enables the identification of various tissues and cell types in the embryo based on differential uptake of tungsten ions.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The μ-CT visualization of embryonic cartilage was validated by directly aligning stained histological sections with the 3D models.
source: We validated the μ-CT visualization of embryonic cartilage by directly aligning stained histological sections with the 3D models (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This describes a validation approach, with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: There is an absence of endochondrial ossifications in the nasal capsule between E14.5–17.5.
source: Note the absence of endochondrial ossifications in the nasal capsule between E14.5–17.5.
evidence: This observation is noted in the figure legend for Figure 1A and supported by the image.

claim: Despite significant anterio-posterior elongation due to synchondroses, synchondroses cannot entirely explain the growth dynamics in all directions: anterio-posterior, latero-medial and dorso-ventral vectors of growth.
source: We analyzed the expansion of the chondrocranium due to synchondroses and found that despite a significant anterio-posterior elongation, synchondroses cannot entirely explain the growth dynamics in all directions: anterio-posterior, latero-medial and dorso-ventral vectors of growth (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of chondrocranium expansion, supported by Figure 1.

claim: A complete absence of synchondroses and other endochondrial ossifications was found in the growing nasal capsule, even at the earliest postnatal stages, while membranous ossifications appeared well developed.
source: Specifically, we found a complete absence of synchondroses and other endochondrial ossifications in the growing nasal capsule, even at the earliest postnatal stages, while membranous ossifications appeared well developed.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: The stereotypical clonal cell dynamics found in synchondroses did not appear during the development of the nasal capsule.
source: The stereotypical clonal cell dynamics found in synchondroses (Figure 1D–I) did not appear during the development of the nasal capsule.
evidence: This is a comparative observation supported by Figure 1.

claim: During the entire embryonic development, chondrocranium growth and shaping is largely aided by additional and unknown mechanisms of growth.
source: Therefore, during the entire embryonic development, chondrocranium growth and shaping is largely aided by additional and unknown mechanisms of growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observations about the nasal capsule.

claim: Genetic tracing in Col2a1-CreERT2/R26Confetti and Sox10-CreERT2/R26Confetti embryos was used to birth-date different regions of the facial cartilage.
source: To understand growth dynamics there, we birth-dated different regions of the facial cartilage using genetic tracing in Col2a1-CreERT2/R26Confetti and Sox10-CreERT2/R26Confetti embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes a methodological approach used in the study.

claim: Both Col2a1-CreERT2 and Sox10-CreERT2 lines recombine in committed chondrocyte progenitors and in mature chondrocytes.
source: Both Col2a1-CreERT2 and Sox10-CreERT2 lines recombine in committed chondrocyte progenitors and in mature chondrocytes.
evidence: This describes the specificity of the genetic tools used.

claim: 3D analysis following tamoxifen injections at different developmental stages allowed identification of the parts of the cartilage that develop from pre-existing chondrocytes and the regions generated from other cellular sources.
source: 3D analysis following tamoxifen injections at different developmental stages allowed us to identify the parts of the cartilage that develop from pre-existing chondrocytes and the regions generated from other cellular sources (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the analytical approach and its outcomes.

claim: Important and relatively large geometrical features are produced from waves of fresh mesenchymal condensations induced directly adjacent to larger pre-laid cartilage elements between E13.5 and E17.5, including the frontal nasal cartilage, nasal concha, labyrinth of ethmoid and cribriform plate.
source: We discovered that important and relatively large geometrical features are produced from waves of fresh mesenchymal condensations induced directly adjacent to larger pre-laid cartilage elements between E13.5 and E17.5: this includes the frontal nasal cartilage, nasal concha, labyrinth of ethmoid and, consistent with previous suggestions, cribriform plate (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K).
evidence: This is a discovery from the genetic tracing experiments, supported by figures.

claim: The complete chondrocranium (including skull base) develops from 14 pairs of early independently induced large cartilaginous elements that fuse together during later development.
source: Our results are complementary to the findings of McBratney-Owen and Morris-Key with coworkers, who demonstrated that the complete chondrocranium (including skull base) develops from 14 pairs of early independently induced large cartilaginous elements that fuse together during later development (McBratney-Owen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work and is complementary to the current findings.

claim: New adjacent mesenchymal condensation can increase the geometrical complexity of a single solid cartilaginous element.
source: Here, we demonstrated how new adjacent mesenchymal condensation can increase the geometrical complexity of a single solid cartilaginous element.
evidence: This is a finding from the study.

claim: The shape of the nasal capsule is generally established by E14.5.
source: The results obtained from comparisons of cartilaginous nasal capsules from different developmental stages showed that the shape of the structure is generally established by E14.5 (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Video 1).
evidence: This is an observation from developmental stage comparisons, supported by figures and video.

claim: From E14.5 until E17.5 the cartilaginous nasal capsule is accurately scaled up with significant geometrical tuning.
source: Nevertheless, from E14.5 until E17.5 the cartilaginous nasal capsule is accurately scaled up with significant geometrical tuning (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is an observation from developmental stage comparisons, supported by Figure 3.

claim: Previous knowledge suggests that the underlying growth mechanism should be based on appositional growth of the cartilage during its transition to bone.
source: Previous knowledge suggests that the underlying growth mechanism should be based on appositional growth of the cartilage during its transition to bone (Hayes et al., 2001; Li et al., 2017), however, numerous facial cartilages never ossify, but continue to grow.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Numerous facial cartilages never ossify, but continue to grow.
source: Previous knowledge suggests that the underlying growth mechanism should be based on appositional growth of the cartilage during its transition to bone (Hayes et al., 2001; Li et al., 2017), however, numerous facial cartilages never ossify, but continue to grow.
evidence: This is an observation that challenges previous assumptions.

claim: Tomographic reconstructions of sheet-shaped cartilage elements in the nasal capsule revealed extensive expansion of the cartilage surface area and overall volume.
source: Tomographic reconstructions of sheet-shaped cartilage elements in the nasal capsule revealed extensive expansion of the cartilage surface area and overall volume (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: This is a finding from tomographic analysis, supported by Figure 3.

claim: The thickness of the cartilaginous sheets did not change as much as the other dimensions during nasal capsule growth.
source: Surprisingly, the thickness of the cartilaginous sheets did not change as much as the other dimensions during nasal capsule growth (Figure 3C–F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Video 1).
evidence: This is a surprising observation from the analysis, supported by figures and video.

claim: The sheet-shaped cartilage expands mostly laterally (within the plane) during directional growth.
source: Thus, the sheet-shaped cartilage expands mostly laterally (within the plane) during directional growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation about thickness versus lateral expansion.

claim: Clonal color-coding and genetic tracing demonstrated transversely oriented clones represented by mostly perpendicular cell columns or clusters formed by traced chondrocytes.
source: Surprisingly, and contrary to this, clonal color-coding and genetic tracing demonstrated transversely oriented clones represented by mostly perpendicular cell columns or clusters formed by traced chondrocytes (Figure 4, especially A-C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a key finding from genetic tracing experiments, supported by Figure 4.

claim: Clonal analysis and color-coding of neural crest-derived chondrogenic and non-chondrogenic ectomesenchyme showed intense mixing of neural crest-derived clones in any given location.
source: Clonal analysis and color-coding of neural crest-derived chondrogenic and non-chondrogenic ectomesenchyme showed intense mixing of neural crest-derived clones in any given location (Figure 4A–C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G) (Kaucka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from clonal analysis, supported by figures and a citation.

claim: Chondrogenic ectomesenchyme demonstrated the presence of transversely oriented doublets of genetically traced and also EdU-labeled cells already at E13.5.
source: At the same time, chondrogenic ectomesenchyme demonstrated the presence of transversely oriented doublets of genetically traced and also EdU-labeled cells already at E13.5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G (inserts) and H).
evidence: This is an observation from early developmental stages, supported by supplementary figures.

claim: Analysis of neural crest progeny in established cartilage highlighted the presence of perpendicularly oriented clonal doublets and columns.
source: Next, analysis of neural crest progeny in established cartilage highlighted the presence of perpendicularly oriented clonal doublets and columns (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from lineage tracing, supported by Figure 4.

claim: Analysis of EdU incorporation and genetic tracing with chondrocyte-specific Col2a1-CreERT2/R26Confetti and Sox10-CreERT2/R26Confetti lines confirmed the existence of transversely oriented products of cell proliferation in the mature (E14.5-E17.5) cartilage.
source: Further analysis of EdU incorporation and genetic tracing with chondrocyte-specific Col2a1-CreERT2/R26Confetti and Sox10-CreERT2/R26Confetti lines confirmed the existence of transversely oriented products of cell proliferation in the mature (E14.5-E17.5) cartilage (Figure 4D–F for EdU, Figure 4G,H–L and Figure 4—figure supplement 2 for lineage tracing).
evidence: This is a confirmation of the finding using multiple approaches, supported by figures.

claim: Cells in the sheet-shaped cartilage do not allocate daughter cells in lateral (longitudinal) dimensions as would be intuitively expected.
source: These results imply that cells in the sheet-shaped cartilage do not allocate daughter cells in lateral (longitudinal) dimensions as would be intuitively expected.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of transverse clonal orientation.

claim: Simple lateral or unidirectional proliferation cannot account for the accurate scaling of the sheet-shaped cartilage in the face.
source: Thus, simple lateral or unidirectional proliferation cannot account for the accurate scaling of the sheet-shaped cartilage in the face.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observations.

claim: The cartilage development from chondrogenic condensations is achieved by a cellular mechanism that involves intercalation of columnar clonal units.
source: Instead, the cartilage development from chondrogenic condensations is achieved by a cellular mechanism that involves intercalation of columnar clonal units.
evidence: This is a main conclusion about the mechanism of cartilage development.

claim: Individual cell dynamics were modelled in silico in 4D (3D + time) to understand possible mechanisms of accurate sheet-shaped cartilage surface development.
source: To better understand possible mechanisms of accurate sheet-shaped cartilage surface development we modelled individual cell dynamics, in silico in 4D (3D + time) (Figure 5) (Hellander, 2015).
evidence: This describes the computational modeling approach used.

claim: The modeling tested a group of variables including: cell division speed, allocation of daughter cells in random- or defined directions, orientation cues in the tissue (equivalent to molecule gradients), as well as pushing/intercalating of the daughter cells during proliferation.
source: We tested a group of variables including: cell division speed, allocation of daughter cells in random- or defined directions, orientation cues in the tissue (equivalent to molecule gradients), as well as pushing/intercalating of the daughter cells during proliferation.
evidence: This describes the parameters tested in the computational model.

claim: The results from in silico simulations were qualitatively compared to experimental clonal analysis from various genetic tracing experiments to identify conditions in the model that were compatible with patterns observed in vivo.
source: We qualitatively compared the results from in silico simulations to our experimental clonal analysis from various genetic tracing experiments, in order to identify conditions in the model that were compatible with patterns observed in vivo.
evidence: This describes the validation approach for the computational model.

claim: The results of the mathematical modelling suggested that the clonal dynamics observed in natural conditions requires polarity cues in the system, specifically, a two-sided gradient of signals would be required to precisely fine-tune cartilage thickness.
source: The results of the mathematical modelling suggested that the clonal dynamics observed in natural conditions requires polarity cues in the system, specifically, a two-sided gradient of signals would be required to precisely fine- tune cartilage thickness (Figure 5A–J).
evidence: This is a key finding from the computational modeling, supported by Figure 5.

claim: Some yet to be identified mechanism controls the average number of cell divisions in a column, further controlling columnar height and undoubtedly regulating the local thickness of the cartilage.
source: At the same time, some yet to be identified mechanism controls the average number of cell divisions in a column, further controlling columnar height and undoubtedly regulating the local thickness of the cartilage.
evidence: This is an inference about an unknown mechanism that needs to be identified.

claim: Combined with the observed introduction of the transverse clonal columns, oriented cell proliferation can provide fine surface generation and scaling.
source: Combined with the observed introduction of the transverse clonal columns, oriented cell proliferation can provide fine surface generation and scaling (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion about the functional outcome of the observed mechanism.

claim: The model highlighted the elegance of cartilage design involving transverse columnar clones in the sheet-shaped elements: this logic enables the uncoupling of thickness control (depends on cell numbers within a clone) and lateral expansion (depends on the number of initiated clones), which are likely two molecularly unrelated processes in vivo.
source: Moreover, the model highlighted the elegance of cartilage design involving transverse columnar clones in the sheet-shaped elements: this logic enables the uncoupling of thickness control (depends on cell numbers within a clone) and lateral expansion (depends on the number of initiated clones), which are likely two molecularly unrelated processes in vivo.
evidence: This is an insight from the modeling about the functional logic of the system.

claim: The absence of a gradient during in silico simulations led to the generation of 3D asymmetrical clusters instead of straight columns.
source: The absence of a gradient during in silico simulations led to the generation of 3D asymmetrical clusters instead of straight columns (even in conditions of highly synchronized cell divisions, and starting from a laterally space-constrained initial configuration - suggesting the promotion of vertical growth due to space-exclusion in the lateral direction) (Figure 5I,J).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational modeling, supported by Figure 5.

claim: The absence of a gradient led to the formation of surface irregularities in the cartilage with subsequent loss of local flatness.
source: This, in turn, led to the formation of surface irregularities in the cartilage with subsequent loss of local flatness (heat-map diagram in Figure 5I,J).
evidence: This is a consequence observed in the modeling, supported by Figure 5.

claim: For cartilaginous structures in the head with asymmetrical or complex irregular geometries, such as areas where several sheet-shaped cartilage elements were merged, clones were not constructed to perpendicular columns.
source: Importantly, lineage tracing also showed that for cartilaginous structures in the head with asymmetrical or complex irregular geometries, such as areas where several sheet-shaped cartilage elements were merged, clones were not constructed to perpendicular columns.
evidence: This is an observation from lineage tracing experiments.

claim: In locations with asymmetrical or complex irregular geometries, irregular clonal clusters or randomly oriented clonal doublets were identified, in accordance with the modelling results.
source: In such locations, we identified irregular clonal clusters or randomly oriented clonal doublets, in accordance with the modelling results (Figure 6A–J).
evidence: This is an observation that validates the modeling predictions, supported by Figure 6.

claim: The shape and orientation of clones corresponds to the local geometry of the cartilage element.
source: Thus, the shape and orientation of clones corresponds to the local geometry of the cartilage element.
evidence: This is a general conclusion drawn from the observations.

claim: Activation of ACVR1 (BMP type one receptor, ALK2) in developing cartilage leads to a phenotype with targeted clonal micro-geometries.
source: Next, we attempted to target a molecular mechanism that controls the flatness and sheet-like shape of the facial cartilaginous sheets. We discovered that activation of ACVR1 (BMP type one receptor, ALK2) in developing cartilage leads to a phenotype with targeted clonal micro-geometries (Figure 6K–P,R).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental manipulation, supported by Figure 6.

claim: Constitutively activated caALK2 transgene resulted in a dramatic change of the shape of clonal envelopes, changing from straight perpendicular columns to disorganized spherical clusters inside the sheet-shaped cartilages.
source: We utilized a constitutively activated caALK2 transgene (Fukuda et al., 2006) together with genetic tracing in a way that every GFP-expressing cell is carrying constitutively active ACVR1. This experiment revealed a dramatic change of the shape of clonal envelopes, changing from straight perpendicular columns to disorganized spherical clusters inside the sheet-shaped cartilages of transgenic Sox10-CreERT2/R26caALK2-IRES-GFP embryos (Figure 6K–N).
evidence: This is a finding from the caALK2 experiment, supported by Figure 6 and a citation.

claim: The ectopically activated ACVR1 resulted in the presence of clonal spherical clusters that interfered with the cartilage borders and caused the formation of ectopic bumps, swellings and other abnormal local shapes.
source: The ectopically activated ACVR1 resulted in the presence of clonal spherical clusters that interfered with the cartilage borders and caused the formation of ectopic bumps, swellings and other abnormal local shapes - in accordance with the mathematical modelling predictions (substantially resembling the condition with no gradient, see Figure 5I) (Figure 6O–P).
evidence: This is a finding from the caALK2 experiment that validates modeling predictions, supported by figures.

claim: All recombined cells in the caALK2 experiment became Sox9+ chondrocytes with no other cell types found to be GFP+, including perichondrial cells.
source: All recombined cells in this caALK2 experiment became Sox9+ chondrocytes. There were no other cell types found to be GFP+, including perichondrial cells.
evidence: This is an observation about cell fate in the caALK2 experiment.

claim: BMP family ligands either produce the gradient that directs the orientated behavior of chondrocytes inside of the cartilage or an experimental increase of BMP signaling renders the cells insensitive to the gradient established by other molecules.
source: This result indicates that BMP family ligands either produce the gradient that directs the orientated behavior of chondrocytes inside of the cartilage or, alternatively, that an experimental increase of BMP signaling renders the cells insensitive to the gradient established by other molecules.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the caALK2 experimental results.

claim: ACVR1 mutation can be used as a tool to change columnar arrangements into clusters.
source: In any case, ACVR1 mutation can be used as a tool to change columnar arrangements into clusters (Figure 6N,R).
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of ACVR1 manipulation, supported by Figure 6.

claim: The activation of ACVR1 by Sox10-CreERT2 starting from E12.5 occurred both in perichondrial cells and in chondrocytes.
source: The activation of ACVR1 by Sox10-CreERT2 starting from E12.5 occurred both in perichondrial cells and in chondrocytes (based on our genetic tracing results using Sox10-CreERT2/R26Confetti).
evidence: This is an observation about the cell types affected by the manipulation.

claim: Clonal bumps and bulging regions were positioned mainly at the surface of sheet-shaped cartilaginous sheets.
source: This later coincided with clonal bumps and bulging regions positioned mainly at the surface of sheet-shaped cartilaginous sheets (Figure 6L,N,P).
evidence: This is an observation from the caALK2 experiment, supported by Figure 6.

claim: Integration of clonal chondrocyte clusters into existing cartilaginous sheets likely depends on clonal shape and originates from the periphery of the cartilage.
source: These data also support the hypothesis that integration of clonal chondrocyte clusters into existing cartilaginous sheets likely depends on clonal shape and originates from the periphery of the cartilage.
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by the caALK2 experimental data.

claim: When the column-inserting process fails, the progeny of cells at the periphery of the cartilage forms ectopic bumps outside of the normal cartilage borders, and disrupts the flatness and straightness of cartilage surfaces.
source: When this column-inserting process fails, the progeny of cells at the periphery of the cartilage forms ectopic bumps outside of the normal cartilage borders, and disrupts the flatness and straightness of cartilage surfaces.
evidence: This is an interpretation of what happens when the normal process is disrupted.

claim: Distinct facial phenotypes have appeared in Ror2, Vangl2 and Wnt5a homozygous mutants.
source: To do this we performed µ-CT and EdU-incorporation analysis on Wnt/PCP mutants. Wnt/PCP pathway is well known for driving the cell and tissue polarity, and distinct facial phenotypes have appeared in Ror2, Vangl2 and Wnt5a homozygous mutants (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is an observation from mutant analysis, supported by Figure 7.

claim: When EdU was administered 24 hr before embryo harvest, subsequent analysis showed no differences in the EdU-positive perpendicular clonal columns which formed within sheet-shaped facial cartilage of Wnt5a knockout mutants or wild type controls.
source: When EdU was administered 24 hr before embryo harvest, subsequent analysis showed no differences in the EdU-positive perpendicular clonal columns which formed within sheet-shaped facial cartilage of Wnt5a knockout mutants or wild type controls (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This is a finding from EdU analysis in Wnt5a mutants, supported by Figure 7.

claim: As early as at E12.5, Wnt5a mutants had abnormal shape and placement of the mesenchymal condensations that create a template for future cartilaginous structures.
source: µ-CT analysis at early developmental stages showed that as early as at E12.5, Wnt5a mutants had abnormal shape and placement of the mesenchymal condensations that create a template for future cartilaginous structures (Figure 7E–F).
evidence: This is a finding from early developmental analysis of Wnt5a mutants, supported by Figure 7.

claim: µ-CT analysis of Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 homozygous mutants at later developmental stages confirmed that chondrocranium shape was heavily affected (with generally shortened nasal capsules as compared to both wild-type and heterozygous controls).
source: Although µ-CT analysis of Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 homozygous mutants at later developmental stages confirmed that chondrocranium shape was heavily affected (with generally shortened nasal capsules as compared to both wild-type and heterozygous controls) (Figure 7A), we did not detect any defects in cartilage micro-geometry, including thickness or surface organization.
evidence: This is a finding from mutant analysis, supported by Figure 7.

claim: No defects were detected in cartilage micro-geometry, including thickness or surface organization, in Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 homozygous mutants.
source: Although µ-CT analysis of Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 homozygous mutants at later developmental stages confirmed that chondrocranium shape was heavily affected (with generally shortened nasal capsules as compared to both wild-type and heterozygous controls) (Figure 7A), we did not detect any defects in cartilage micro-geometry, including thickness or surface organization.
evidence: This is a negative finding from mutant analysis.

claim: Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 do not control cartilage growth and shaping per se (via the insertion of perpendicular columns).
source: Altogether, these results indicate that Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 do not control cartilage growth and shaping per se (via the insertion of perpendicular columns).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutant analysis.

claim: Wnt5a, Ror2 and Vangl2 influence the position and shape of chondrogenic condensations, which define the future geometry of the facial chondrocranium.
source: Instead, they influence the position and shape of chondrogenic condensations, which define the future geometry of the facial chondrocranium (Figure 7E,F).
evidence: This is a conclusion about the role of Wnt/PCP genes, supported by Figure 7.

claim: Inactivation of Gsα, encoded by Gnas, is known to lead to accelerated differentiation of columnar chondrocytes, without affecting other aspects of cartilage biology.
source: Knowing from our results that proliferation rate drops in the mature cartilage, we hypothesized that chondrocyte maturation speed may influence the number of cell divisions within a column. To test this suggestion, we analyzed G-protein stimulatory α-subunit (Gsα) knockout embryos (Figure 8). Inactivation of Gsα, encoded by Gnas, is known to lead to accelerated differentiation of columnar chondrocytes, without affecting other aspects of cartilage biology (Chagin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A significant reduction of cartilage thickness in absolute metrics was observed in three different locations in the developing chondrocrania of Gsα knockout embryos.
source: We analyzed three different locations in the developing chondrocrania, and observed a significant reduction of cartilage thickness in absolute metrics (Figure 8A,B,J), as well as in terms of the number of cells within each column (Figure 8B–H).
evidence: This is a finding from the Gsα knockout analysis, supported by Figure 8.

claim: A significant reduction in the number of cells within each column was observed in Gsα knockout embryos.
source: We analyzed three different locations in the developing chondrocrania, and observed a significant reduction of cartilage thickness in absolute metrics (Figure 8A,B,J), as well as in terms of the number of cells within each column (Figure 8B–H).
evidence: This is a finding from the Gsα knockout analysis, supported by Figure 8.

claim: Sheet-shaped cartilages in Gsα knockout embryos are thinner than that of littermate controls, while other parameters (including general size and shape of nasal capsule and other locations in the head together with the transverse orientation of chondrocyte columns) remain largely unaffected.
source: The result of this experiment demonstrated that sheet-shaped cartilages in Gsα knockout embryos are thinner than that of littermate controls, while other parameters (including general size and shape of nasal capsule and other locations in the head together with the transverse orientation of chondrocyte columns) remain largely unaffected (Figure 8A,B,I).
evidence: This is a finding from the Gsα knockout analysis, supported by Figure 8.

claim: The Gsα knockout data experimentally validated mathematical predictions and confirmed that the thickness of cartilage is determined by the number of cell divisions within a transverse clone, and that this is uncoupled from lateral expansion.
source: Thus, these data experimentally validated mathematical predictions and confirmed that the thickness of cartilage is determined by the number of cell divisions within a transverse clone, and that this is uncoupled from lateral expansion.
evidence: This is a conclusion that validates the modeling predictions using experimental data.

claim: Clonal genetic tracing of chondrocyte progenitors and chondrocytes in Meckel, rib and limb cartilages showed that the clonal arrangements appeared highly oriented and strongly resembled the clonal columns observed in the facial cartilage.
source: Next, we wanted to know how clonal cell dynamics accounts for the shape development in rod-shaped cartilages. For this we investigated the clonal dynamics in Meckel, rib and limb cartilages with the help of Confetti-based genetic tracing as well as EdU incorporation. The clonal arrangements appeared highly oriented and strongly resembled the clonal columns we observed in the facial cartilage.
evidence: This is a finding from clonal analysis in rod-shaped cartilages.

claim: The columnar clones in rod-shaped cartilages were oriented mostly transversally in the plane of a rod diameter and could not explain the early growth along the main axis of the skeletal element.
source: The columnar clones were oriented mostly transversally in the plane of a rod diameter and could not explain the early growth along the main axis of the skeletal element (Figure 9).
evidence: This is an observation from clonal analysis in rod-shaped cartilages, supported by Figure 9.

claim: Longitudinal extension of rod-shaped cartilages is based on continuous development of chondrogenic mesenchymal condensations on the distal tip and is followed by the transverse proliferation of chondrocytes, which accounts for the proper diameter of a cartilaginous rod.
source: These tracing results suggested that longitudinal extension is based on continuous development of chondrogenic mesenchymal condensations on the distal tip and is followed by the transverse proliferation of chondrocytes, which accounts for the proper diameter of a cartilaginous rod.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clonal tracing results in rod-shaped cartilages.

claim: Starting from E14.5, the olfactory capsule is already formed of mature chondrocytes.
source: Since the integration of clonal units is likely to be uneven in the cartilage, we questioned how the anisotropy of local proliferation can impact the shaping processes on a macro-scale. Starting from E14.5, the olfactory capsule is already formed of mature chondrocytes.
evidence: This is an observation about the developmental state of the olfactory capsule.

claim: In the olfactory capsule, proliferation was localized to specific regions, but remained generally low elsewhere according to the analysis of EdU incorporation.
source: Indeed, in this structure, proliferation was localized to specific regions, but remained generally low elsewhere (Figure 11A–B) according to the analysis of EdU incorporation.
evidence: This is a finding from EdU incorporation analysis, supported by Figure 11.

claim: Proliferative regions expand due to the active integration of new clonal columns and clusters.
source: As we demonstrated above, proliferative regions expand due to the active integration of new clonal columns and clusters.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on previous observations.

claim: Since proliferative zones in nasal capsule are restricted and have defined edges, they inevitably induce tension and bending of the surrounding cartilage sheet.
source: Since proliferative zones in nasal capsule are restricted and have defined edges, they inevitably induce tension and bending of the surrounding cartilage sheet.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanical consequences of localized proliferation.

claim: In silico modeling of nasal capsule shape transition from E13.5 to E14.5 showed that two lateral zones with a low rate of proliferation impose a characteristic bending on the sides of the simulated structure.
source: To simulate in silico nasal capsule shape transition from E13.5 to E14.5, we generated a basic E13.5-like shape by converting a sheet-shaped growing trapezoid into a corresponding 3D structure (Figure 12A, central part and Video 2). The result was considered as a simplified starting condition for further simulations. Next, two lateral zones with a low rate of proliferation were introduced according to their original position in E13.5 nasal capsule. Further simulations of the growth showed that these low proliferative zones impose a characteristic bending on the sides of the simulated structure.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling, supported by Figure 12 and Video 2.

claim: The characteristic lateral bending observed in modeling corresponds to the lateral transformations observed in embryonic development of the nasal capsule between E13.5 and E14.5.
source: This bending corresponds to the lateral transformations observed in embryonic development of the nasal capsule between E13.5 and E14.5 (Figure 12B–C).
evidence: This is a validation of the modeling results against biological observations, supported by Figure 12.

claim: According to the model, the characteristic lateral bending did not depend on anterio-posterior polarity in the cartilage or formation of the groove at the midline.
source: This characteristic lateral bending did not depend on anterio-posterior polarity in the cartilage or formation of the groove at the midline (Figure 12D).
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling about what factors are not required for lateral bending, supported by Figure 12.

claim: According to the model, the polarity only affected the potential for the anterior elongation due to the anisotropic growth of the entire cartilaginous structure.
source: According to the model, the polarity only affected the potential for the anterior elongation due to the anisotropic growth of the entire cartilaginous structure.
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling about the role of polarity.

claim: The nasal septum functions as a slower proliferating anchoring point to the roof of the nasal capsule, which is necessary for the formation of the midline groove at E14.5.
source: Our results also suggested that the nasal septum functions as a slower proliferating anchoring point to the roof of the nasal capsule, which is necessary for the formation of the midline groove at E14.5.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling results.

claim: A simulated groove at the midline provided for the general bend and flattened shape of the in silico cartilage, similar to the native E14.5 nasal capsule and contrary to the model without the simulated midline groove.
source: A simulated groove at the midline provided for the general bend and flattened shape of the in silico cartilage, similar to the native E14.5 nasal capsule and contrary to the model without the simulated midline groove (Figure 12C–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling, supported by Figure 12.

claim: Material modelling using plastic film demonstrated that growth zones/local expansions in the flat planes generate mechanical tensions which bend the structure.
source: To validate the general rules of in silico transformations, we performed material modelling using plastic film to simulate anisotropic expansion and bending due to integration of local growing zones with attached borders. This simple material modeling demonstrated that growth zones/local expansions in the flat planes generate mechanical tensions which bend the structure (Figure 12E).
evidence: This is a finding from physical material modeling, supported by Figure 12.

claim: Material modelling using isotropic thermal expansion/constriction of a plastic film with black regions (analogous to the lateral low proliferative zones in E13.5 nasal capsule) created physical tensions that eventually bent the structure in a way similar to the original nasal capsule geometry at E14.5.
source: We then performed another material modelling experiment using isotropic thermal expansion/constriction of a plastic film. For this purpose, we drew black regions (analogous to the lateral low proliferative zones in E13.5 nasal capsule) onto white plastic film that was cut in a shape of a trapezoid capable of transforming into a nasal capsule-like dome. Under the heating provided by a thermal infrared lamp, the black zones received more heat and isotropically shrunk. Shrinkage of the black zones created physical tensions that eventually bent the structure in a way similar to the original nasal capsule geometry at E14.5 (Figure 12F).
evidence: This is a finding from physical material modeling, supported by Figure 12.

claim: The distribution of uneven proliferative zones plays an important role in the shaping of the facial chondrocranium during embryonic development.
source: These results, combined with analysis of proliferation and 3D visualizations, strongly suggest that the distribution of uneven proliferative zones plays an important role in the shaping of the facial chondrocranium during embryonic development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: A set of principles contributing to the accurate scaling and shaping of cartilage tissue during growth has been revealed.
source: Taken together, we reveal a set of principles contributing to the accurate scaling and shaping of cartilage tissue during growth.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: The reverse engineering of the cartilage growth process highlights the involvement of highly specialized systems that control the directional growth at the levels of micro- (clonal shapes) and macro-geometries (proliferative regions in nasal capsule).
source: The reverse engineering of this process highlights the involvement of highly specialized systems that control the directional growth at the levels of micro- (clonal shapes) and macro-geometries (proliferative regions in nasal capsule).
evidence: This is a summary of the multi-scale findings.

claim: Allometric growth of complex 3D cartilage elements is not achieved by simple, evenly distributed and/or unidirectional proliferation, but is sculpted by precisely localized proliferation.
source: Our results show that allometric growth of complex 3D cartilage elements is not achieved by simple, evenly distributed and/or unidirectional proliferation, but is sculpted by precisely localized proliferation.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Previously, the use of chimeric avian embryos demonstrated the competence of facial mesenchyme in producing species-specific shapes and sizes of cartilage elements.
source: Previously, the use of chimeric avian embryos demonstrated the competence of facial mesenchyme in producing species-specific shapes and sizes of cartilage elements (Eames and Schneider, 2008), while facial epithelium and brain provided the instructive signals guiding generalized shaping of the face (Chong et al., 2012; Foppiano et al., 2007; Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Facial epithelium and brain provided the instructive signals guiding generalized shaping of the face.
source: Previously, the use of chimeric avian embryos demonstrated the competence of facial mesenchyme in producing species-specific shapes and sizes of cartilage elements (Eames and Schneider, 2008), while facial epithelium and brain provided the instructive signals guiding generalized shaping of the face (Chong et al., 2012; Foppiano et al., 2007; Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Knowledge of how the facial cartilaginous elements are shaped has been rather restricted, and mainly concerned with the correct formation of chondrogenic mesenchymal condensations.
source: Knowledge of how the facial cartilaginous elements are shaped has been rather restricted, and mainly concerned with the correct formation of chondrogenic mesenchymal condensations.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in previous knowledge.

claim: Anisotropic proliferation and oriented clonal cell dynamics are implemented to achieve accurate expansion of the chondrogenic condensation or cartilage during growth.
source: The accurate expansion of the chondrogenic condensation or cartilage during growth is no trivial matter. The general shape should be both preserved and modified at the same time. We show that anisotropic proliferation and oriented clonal cell dynamics are implemented to achieve the necessary outcome.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study.

claim: Allometric growth of complex 3D structures requires certain cellular logics and cannot efficiently proceed with equally distributed and/or unidirectional proliferation inside of the mesenchymal condensation or cartilage element.
source: Allometric growth of complex 3D structures requires certain cellular logics and cannot efficiently proceed with equally distributed and/or unidirectional proliferation inside of the mesenchymal condensation or cartilage element.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings.

claim: The formation of growth plate-like zones in early sheet-shaped (nasal capsule) or rod-shaped cartilages, nor uniform expansion of cartilage in all directions was not observed.
source: On the other hand, we did not observe the formation of growth plate-like zones in early sheet-shaped (nasal capsule) or rod-shaped cartilages, nor uniform expansion of cartilage in all directions.
evidence: This is a negative observation from the study.

claim: A model simulating different aspects of multicellular dynamics in 3D together with lineage tracing of individual clones was devised to test various strategies of cellular behavior during cartilage growth.
source: To test various strategies of cellular behavior during cartilage growth we devised a model simulating different aspects of multicellular dynamics in 3D together with lineage tracing of individual clones.
evidence: This describes the modeling approach used.

claim: Most of the currently existing models of cell dynamics and tracing operate in 2D space, which often limits the predictions.
source: Most of the currently existing models of cell dynamics and tracing operate in 2D space, which often limits the predictions (Jarjour et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and provides context for the modeling approach.

claim: The model suggested that a gradient-controlled orientation of clonal expansion can explain the biological observations and showed the relation between the geometries of clonal domains (envelopes), the overall shape and the fineness of the surface.
source: Our model suggested that a gradient-controlled orientation of clonal expansion can explain the biological observations (i.e. it is consistent with ordered columnar growth and its disruption results in spherical microdomains rather than columns), and showed the relation between the geometries of clonal domains (envelopes), the overall shape and the fineness of the surface.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational modeling.

claim: The predictions from the model were confirmed in a series of experiments involving tracing with multicolor reporters and manipulating the cartilage with mutations.
source: We confirmed the predictions from the model in a series of experiments involving tracing with multicolor reporters and manipulating the cartilage with mutations.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation of the model.

claim: The formation of oriented clones of chondrocytes with clonal envelope shape corresponds to the geometry of the analyzed locality.
source: Our results showed that the formation of oriented clones of chondrocytes with clonal envelope shape corresponds to the geometry of the analyzed locality.
evidence: This is a main finding from the experimental work.

claim: The sheet-shaped cartilage elements consisted of transversely oriented clonal columns, while asymmetric complex geometries revealed a variety of clonal shapes ranging from spherical to particularly oriented.
source: The sheet-shaped cartilage elements consisted of transversely oriented clonal columns, while asymmetric complex geometries revealed a variety of clonal shapes ranging from spherical to particularly oriented.
evidence: This is a finding about the relationship between cartilage geometry and clonal shapes.

claim: Genetic tracing initiated during transition of condensations into cartilage resulted in clonal columns within both sheet- and rod-shaped cartilage elements.
source: Genetic tracing initiated during transition of condensations into cartilage resulted in clonal columns within both sheet- and rod-shaped cartilage elements.
evidence: This is a finding from genetic tracing experiments.

claim: Chondrogenic condensations undergo complex oriented cell dynamics during their development.
source: This confirms that chondrogenic condensations undergo complex oriented cell dynamics during their development.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the genetic tracing results.

claim: Tracing of chondrocranium cartilage showed formation of transverse clonal columns as growth proceeded.
source: Importantly, tracing of chondrocranium cartilage showed formation of transverse clonal columns as growth proceeded.
evidence: This is a finding from genetic tracing experiments.

claim: Intercalation of newly born columns into pre-existing cartilage provided for the expansion potential in the sheet-shaped cartilage.
source: Intercalation of newly born columns into pre-existing cartilage provided for the expansion potential in the sheet-shaped cartilage.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the mechanism of cartilage expansion.

claim: This growth mechanism is very original and is not reported elsewhere so far.
source: This growth mechanism is very original and is not reported elsewhere so far.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: A few studies have demonstrated how clonal envelopes form in accordance with the general shape of the structure, mainly conducted on Drosophila imaginal wing disc or growing flower petals.
source: A few studies have demonstrated how clonal envelopes form in accordance with the general shape of the structure. These were mainly conducted on Drosophila imaginal wing disc or growing flower petals.
evidence: This provides context from previous studies in other systems.

claim: In all cases the authors highlighted that the shape of clonal geometries correlates with the major vector of expansion in the growing structure.
source: In all cases the authors highlighted that the shape of clonal geometries correlates with the major vector of expansion in the growing structure (Green et al., 2010; Repiso et al., 2013; Strutt, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The presence of polarized activity directs the shaping of the tissue.
source: This implies the presence of polarized activity that directs the shaping of the tissue.
evidence: This is an inference from previous studies.

claim: The first experimental evidence of how the control of the directional clonal expansion influences the shape of a vertebrate tissue on a large scale was provided.
source: Here, we provided the first experimental evidence of how the control of the directional clonal expansion influences the shape of a vertebrate tissue on a large scale.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty and significance of the findings.

claim: In the sheet-shaped cartilage the orientation of clonal domains, i.e. the columns, does not correspond to the vectors of major expansion, but rather serves for uncoupling lateral expansion control and thickness tuning.
source: Moreover, in the sheet-shaped cartilage the orientation of clonal domains, i.e. the columns, does not correspond to the vectors of major expansion, but rather serves for uncoupling lateral expansion control and thickness tuning.
evidence: This is a key insight about the functional logic of the system.

claim: The number of chondrocytes comprising the clonal column or cluster depends on Gsα-mediated signals.
source: In line with that, the number of chondrocytes comprising the clonal column or cluster depends on Gsα-mediated signals.
evidence: This is a finding from the Gsα knockout experiments.

claim: Variations in the number of chondrocytes in a column do not significantly affect the lateral dimensions of the whole sheet-shaped cartilage structure: the thickness of the cartilage becomes less while the general geometry and size stay preserved.
source: Variations in this number do not significantly affect the lateral dimensions of the whole sheet-shaped cartilage structure: the thickness of the cartilage becomes less while the general geometry and size stay preserved.
evidence: This is a finding from the Gsα knockout experiments demonstrating uncoupling of thickness and lateral dimensions.

claim: The shape and orientation of clonal envelopes in cartilage is partially controlled by BMP signaling, since micro-geometries of clones depend on activation of ACVR1.
source: Additionally, the shape and orientation of clonal envelopes in cartilage is partially controlled by BMP signaling, since micro-geometries of clones depend on activation of ACVR1.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the caALK2 experiments.

claim: BMP ligands (because of cAlk2/ACVR1 phenotype affected clonal orientation) expressed around the regularly shaped cartilages may play a role similar to the in silico predicted gradients.
source: Based on these results, we assume that BMP ligands (because of cAlk2/ACVR1 phenotype affected clonal orientation) expressed around the regularly shaped cartilages may play a role similar to the in silico predicted gradients.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental results.

claim: The expression of INHBA, BMP5 and BMP3 fit the expression profile of being expressed around regularly shaped cartilages quite well according to Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas and Eurexpress in situ public databases.
source: Indeed, the expression of INHBA, BMP5 and BMP3 fit this expression profile quite well (according to Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas (http://developingmouse.brain-map.org) and Eurexpress (http://www.eurexpress.org) in situ public databases).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to public databases.

claim: BMP5 is clearly expressed at the cartilage periphery and has been shown to affect the cartilage shape by David Kingsley lab.
source: At least, BMP5 is clearly expressed at the cartilage periphery and has been shown to affect the cartilage shape by David Kingsley lab (Guenther et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Experimental manipulations of planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway did not affect microgeometries and clonal domains, but strongly affected the chondrocranium shape on the macroscopical scale in several different ways.
source: Our experimental manipulations of planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway did not affect microgeometries and clonal domains, but strongly affected the chondrocranium shape on the macroscopical scale in several different ways.
evidence: This is a finding from the Wnt/PCP mutant experiments.

claim: The phenotypes in Wnt/PCP mutants appeared to be rooted in pre-chondrogenic or early chondrogenic stages, and are based on distorted placement of mesenchymal condensations in the very early head.
source: These phenotypes appeared to be rooted in pre-chondrogenic or early chondrogenic stages, and are based on distorted placement of mesenchymal condensations in the very early head.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the developmental timing of Wnt/PCP effects.

claim: Experiments with Wnt/PCP mutants may potentially provide a better understanding of species-specific mechanisms of control and evolution of the facial shape on a macro scale.
source: These experiments with Wnt/PCP mutants may potentially provide a better understanding of species-specific mechanisms of control and evolution of the facial shape on a macro scale.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential implications of the findings.

claim: Regular shapes require regular cellular arrangements and clonal cell dynamics.
source: Regular shapes require regular cellular arrangements and clonal cell dynamics.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the findings.

claim: Rod-shaped cartilage (Meckel, embryonic ribs and long cartilages in limbs) has a regular shape.
source: It is not only sheet-shaped cartilage in the head that demonstrate geometric regularity; rod-shaped cartilage (Meckel, embryonic ribs and long cartilages in limbs) also has a regular shape.
evidence: This is an observation about cartilage geometry.

claim: Regular clonal patterns, conceptually similar to those found in sheet-shaped cartilage, explain conservative tissue dynamics during formation and growth of cartilaginous rods.
source: Regular clonal patterns, conceptually similar to those found in sheet-shaped cartilage, explain conservative tissue dynamics during formation and growth of cartilaginous rods.
evidence: This is a conclusion about rod-shaped cartilage based on the findings.

claim: Formation of clonal columns is important for the diameter control in rod-shaped cartilages, while chondrogenic condensations at the very tip of the rod-shaped growing structures enable elongation.
source: Indeed, genetic tracing experiments suggested that formation of clonal columns is important for the diameter control, while chondrogenic condensations at the very tip of the rod-shaped growing structures enable elongation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from genetic tracing experiments in rod-shaped cartilages.

claim: The mechanism in rod-shaped cartilages may provide for uncoupling of length versus diameter control.
source: Similar to the cell dynamics in the sheet-shaped cartilage, this mechanism may provide for uncoupling of length versus diameter control.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional logic of the mechanism in rod-shaped cartilages.

claim: Such uncoupling may generally enable developmental and evolutional plasticity of cartilage size and shape.
source: Such uncoupling may generally enable developmental and evolutional plasticity of cartilage size and shape.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the evolutionary implications.

claim: The mechanism controlling the thickness or diameter of sheet-shaped and rod-shaped cartilage elements not only includes spatially orientated behavior, but also involves the regulation of cell number within each chondrogenic clone.
source: The mechanism controlling the thickness or diameter of sheet-shaped and rod-shaped cartilage elements not only includes spatially orientated behavior, but also involves the regulation of cell number within each chondrogenic clone.
evidence: This is a summary of the multi-level control mechanism.

claim: Immature chondrocytes are proliferatively active, while more mature chondrocytes show decreased proliferation.
source: Immature chondrocytes are proliferatively active, while more mature chondrocytes show decreased proliferation.
evidence: This is an observation about chondrocyte behavior.

claim: Differentiation speed emerges as a concept which could regulate the organ shape by impinging on clone size, thereby altering the thickness or diameter of the cartilage.
source: Therefore, differentiation speed emerges as a concept which could regulate the organ shape by impinging on clone size, thereby altering the thickness or diameter of the cartilage.
evidence: This is a conceptual conclusion from the observations.

claim: This concept is known to operate in the brain and other tissues with classical stem cell/transiently amplifying cell arrangements.
source: This concept is known to operate in the brain and other tissues with classical stem cell/transiently amplifying cell arrangements (Díaz-Flores et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Clonal genetic tracing and EdU labeling experiments suggested that the origin of clonal columns and clusters might be represented by the cells located at the periphery of forming cartilage.
source: Clonal genetic tracing and EdU labeling experiments suggested that the origin of clonal columns and clusters might be represented by the cells located at the periphery of forming cartilage.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on experimental observations.

claim: The spherical clusters of chondrocytes forming at the periphery of the cartilage in cALK2 mutant mice may suggest that the cell source is also located at the periphery and might be a perichondrial cell.
source: The spherical clusters of chondrocytes forming at the periphery of the cartilage in cALK2 mutant mice may suggest that the cell source is also located at the periphery and might be a perichondrial cell.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the caALK2 experimental observations.

claim: Clonal relationships between perichondrial cells and columns of chondrocytes support the hypothesis of perichondrial cells acting as a stem population during cartilage expansion.
source: Clonal relationships between perichondrial cells and columns of chondrocytes also support the hypothesis of perichondrial cells acting as a stem population during cartilage expansion.
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by clonal tracing observations.

claim: The heterogeneity and multipotency of perichondrial cells is still unclear, although there are multiple studies showing the perichondrium as a source of chondrocytes and osteoblasts.
source: In general, the heterogeneity and multipotency of perichondrial cells is still unclear, although there are multiple studies showing the perichondrium as a source of chondrocytes and osteoblasts (Kobayashi et al., 2011; Li et al., 2017; Maes et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: The perichondrium might mediate non-autonomous effects in the cartilage in case of cAlk2 and GSα experiments.
source: In addition to this, the perichondrium might mediate non-autonomous effects in the cartilage in case of cAlk2 and GSα experiments.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential indirect effects.

claim: Genetic tracing shows that some perichondrial cells always recombine with Sox10-, Plp1- and Col2a1-CreERT2 lines, and, in case of functional experiments, may indirectly control some events in more mature layers.
source: Genetic tracing shows that some perichondrial cells always recombine with Sox10-, Plp1- and Col2a1-CreERT2 lines, and, in case of functional experiments, may indirectly control some evens in more mature layers.
evidence: This is an observation from genetic tracing that raises the possibility of indirect effects.

claim: It is not clear how the fine border of the cartilage is set, and whether the perichondrial layer may play a key border-setting role during development and regeneration.
